newsitem.title: BURUNDI: 20,000 Burundian refugees return from Zaire, WFP.
newsitem.headline: 20,000 Burundian refugees return from Zaire, WFP.

text.p: A total of 20,000 Burundian Hutu refugees have returned home from east Zaire but have little water and food in northwestern Burundi, the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said on Friday.

The refugees were found at Buganda commune near the border with Zaire in the troubled province of Cibitoke during a trip to the region by U.N agencies heavily guarded by Burundi's Tutsi -dominated army.
"We are talking about 20,000 refugees who have come back spontaneously from Zaire," Jean-Luc Siblot, WFP's Burundi representative, who went on the exploratory trip to Cibitoke, told Reuters.

"We need a quick intervention in terms of food, non-food and in terms of health and if it does not happen I don't know how they will survive the next few weeks," he said. "They have been put into four camps by the authorities but security does not allow for them to be fed so they have just been feeding themselves."

Siblot said up to 3,000 other returnees from Zaire, trucked back to Cibitoke's Rugombo commune this week from a transit centre at Gatumba near the capital Bujumbura, were living in "absolutely terrible" conditions with no access to clean water.
Some 140,000 Burundian Hutu refugees fled camps north of the eastern Zairean town of Uvira three weeks ago because of fighting between ethnic Tutsi rebels and the Zairean army.
